newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM's party elects new leader.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM's party elects new leader.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party said on Sunday it had elected a new leader one day after the previous incumbent split the party to head a breakaway group.

Former Textiles Minister Sharad Yadav, from the populous eastern state of Bihar, was voted in as the new president of Janata Dal, which heads India's ruling 15-party United Front coalition, officials said.
Laloo Yadav, no relation of Sharad Yadav but a fellow low-caste leader from Bihar, was party president until Saturday, when his supporters launched the breakaway Rashtriya (national) Janata Dal.
Laloo Yadav had boycotted Thursday's election for party president, saying voter lists had been rigged to favour his challenger, who had a virtual walkover after Saturday's split in the party.
The split posed no threat to Gujral's two-month-old minority coalition. The breakaway group still supports the national government.
Sharad Yadav polled 691 votes against 58 votes for Laloo Prasad Yadav, party general secretary Bapu Kaldate told Reuters. Nine votes were declared invalid.
More than 100 party workers and supporters of Sharad Yadav celebrated his victory in front of the party office in New Delhi beating drums, dancing and shouting slogans.
The centre-left Janata Dal's elections last week were the first since its formation in 1988.

It had until Saturday 45 lawmakers in the 545-seat lower house, Lok Sabha, in which the United Front has an overall 178 members, most of whom belong to regional groups or leftist allies. The split took away 18 lawmakers, including three government ministers.

The ruling coalition is also supported by the Congress party, whose 140 deputies offer make-or-break support to the government in an axis formed to keep out the Hindu nationalists, who control 194 votes.
Laloo Yadav's differences are with former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Sharad Yadav, mainly linked to personality clashes and ambitions.
Laloo Yadav is also embroiled in a $280-million scandal over alleged diversion of animal welfare funds in Bihar.
Yadav, who says he is innocent, refused to resign and face trial after the federal police indicted him.
